title: Standard and extended ACLs: filtering by source, destination, port and protocol

videos.script: A router's access list is a firewall with no memory, bound to one interface. It is cheap enough to run on every port, and it is where most network engineers first meet filtering. {{acl}} In this lesson you will write two in Cisco's notation and run each one on the branch router. A standard list, which only knows who sent a packet. And an extended one, which knows where it is going and on what port. {{two}} You will work out wildcard masks, the inverted way these lists write a network. {{wildcard}} Then where a list belongs, and why a standard list in the wrong place cuts a machine off from everything. {{placement}} Last, the keyword that lets replies back in, and the kind of packet it lets through with them. {{established}}
